content.text: Software testing is the disciplined practice of verifying that code behaves correctly under expected conditions, edge cases, and failure scenarios. In production systems, testing is not an afterthought — it is the engineering discipline that enables teams to ship with confidence, refactor without fear, and maintain velocity as codebases grow to millions of lines.

A robust testing strategy spans multiple levels of abstraction. Unit tests verify individual functions and classes in isolation. Integration tests confirm that components collaborate correctly across boundaries like databases, APIs, and message queues. Property-based tests explore vast input spaces to uncover edge cases that example-based tests miss. The test architecture — how tests are organized, executed, and maintained — determines whether a test suite remains an asset or becomes a liability. And mocking strategies control the boundaries between units, enabling fast feedback loops without sacrificing confidence.

Modern testing goes beyond "does it work?" to answer "will it keep working?" Flaky tests erode trust. Slow suites block deployments. Poorly structured tests couple to implementation details and break on every refactor. This section covers the principles, patterns, and production-grade techniques that separate effective test suites from ceremonial ones.

items: Unit Testing — Test structure, assertions, mocking fundamentals, TDD cycle, and coverage metrics
Integration Testing — Database testing, API testing, contract testing, and test containers
Property-Based Testing — Generators, shrinking, invariants, and stateful testing patterns
Test Architecture — Test pyramid, CI integration, flaky test management, and test organization
Mocking Strategies — When to mock, test doubles taxonomy, dependency injection, and anti-patterns
